sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Graphic shows dilated, tortuous varicose veins of the pampiniform plexus in the spermatic cord and along the posterosuperior aspect of the testis .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Oblique grayscale ultrasound through the cord, in supine position with normal respiration, shows a dilated, tortuous principal vein in the pampiniform plexus measuring 7.5 mm in caliber.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal color Doppler ultrasound of the scrotum in a 24-year-old man shows flow in several dilated veins during Valsalva, indicative of moderate varicocele. Blood flow in the varicocele is slow and may be detected only with low Doppler settings.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Catheter venogram demonstrates a prominent left gonadal vein extending into the left hemiscrotum in this patient with varicocele and infertility. Varicocele resolved after coil embolization.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse US of the left scrotum with the patient at rest in supine position shows multiple anechoic, tubular structures medial to the testis, consistent with varicocele.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal color Doppler US in the same patient during Valsalva shows flow throughout the varicocele due to reflux.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal color Doppler US shows dilated veins with minimal flow at rest . With Valsalva , aliasing is seen due to increased velocity of retrograde blood flow exceeding the low Doppler scale.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Graphic shows normal pampiniform plexus veins compared to abnormally dilated veins in a varicocele .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse US inferior to the testis shows a large, right-sided varicocele . Some of the veins are echogenic due to slow flow (mobile in real time). The patient underwent CT, which was negative. Right-sided varicoceles, without other symptoms of malignancy, are rarely associated with an underlying malignancy.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal US of the spermatic cord just superior to the testis in a patient with palpable, painful area shows a thrombosed varicocele vein as a echogenic, expanded vein without color flow.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT in a patient with history of severe necrotizing pancreatitis shows large, dilated veins in the left hemiscrotum , consistent with varicocele. These communicate with the spermatic (gonadal) vein .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT in the same patient shows a dilated spermatic vein entering a small left renal vein .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in the same patient shows chronic thrombosis of the left renal vein due to past pancreatitis. Rarely, secondary causes of varicocele include vascular thromboses, iatrogenic causes, and tumor compression/venous invasion.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal color Doppler US of the left scrotum in a 20-year-old symptomatic patient shows dilated vessels with scattered Doppler signal at rest.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal color Doppler US in the same patient with Valsalva shows increased size of vessels and marked increase in flow due to retrograde flow in the pampiniform plexus.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-11

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Anterior projection venogram in the same patient after coil embolization of the varicocele shows lack of reflux caudal to the coil mass .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-12

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse color Doppler US shows tortuous, hypoechoic structures in the testis at the mediastinum with minimal flow. Rarely, a varicocele extends into or occurs primarily in the testis. This should not be confused with dilation of the rete testis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse US of both testes shows multiple hypoechoic, tubular structures along the medial aspect of the left testis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-14

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal US of the left scrotum in the same patient shows the tubular and serpiginous nature of the lesion .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-15

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Color Doppler US in the same patient with Valsalva shows marked blood flow , consistent with a moderate-sized varicocele.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal US of the right scrotum in the setting of a palpable mass shows an isolated, right-sided varicocele . Further work-up showed no malignancy. In the past, this was thought to be highly associated with malignancy; however, more recent experience shows that isolated, right-sided varicocele is rarely associated with malignancy. When it does occur in the setting of malignancy, there are often other concerning symptoms.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-17

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Color Doppler US in an older man with scrotal discomfort shows a huge left varicocele. The late onset prompted imaging of the retroperitoneum, which showed marked dilatation of the cava and renal veins due to severe right heart dysfunction.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-18

downloadSentinel:
Varicocele Anki Export

Core validation used the uploaded Core Radiology, Second Edition: GU pages 291–292, Vascular page 573, and IR page 626. These sections support the ultrasound findings, epidemiology, primary-versus-secondary framework, treatment indications, and embolization content.

The validated export contains 39 cards, exactly 39 physical TSV lines, and 22 columns per line. All 22 source images are accounted for across 15 atomic case blocks, with no exclusions. Caption-verbatim, trigger-integrity, cardinality, source-coverage, and deck-balance audits passed.

The RadPrimer and STATdx image binaries were not present locally and are therefore not embedded in the ZIP. The manifest preserves their exact RP-/SDX-qualified filenames, source URLs, case clusters, and verbatim captions for retrieval with source-platform access.
